_comment: Only measured or design-fixed facts for the demo dashboard (host/web/index.html). Update after each measurement; never put estimates here without saying so.
system: 16x16 INT8 weight-stationary systolic array, on-chip K-tile accumulator, 128 KB input replay buffer
RISC-V U54 x4 (app + 3 workers for the CPU layers), bare metal
FastDepth 4.03 MB, MiDaS small 16.8 MB, INT8 in DDR, sent over UART once per power-up
hardware: 126 / 308 (accumulator 1024 x 512 bit, X replay buffer 8192 x 128 bit, FIFOs)
Timing at 50 MHz (static timing, all corners)
MET: worst setup slack +3.20 ns, no hold violations
Fmax of the NPU clock domain (static timing)
hardware_note: Libero SoC 2026.1, place-and-route of 5 Oct (NPU v1.3 with the X replay buffer). The bring-up build (reference design + APB probe) used 12,744 4LUT / 9,066 DFF / 23 LSRAM / 0 math.
verification: RTL shell + accumulator + replay sim (N=4/16, 3 depths)
Real model layers through the RTL (enc0, enc1pw, enc3pw, Canny)
Firmware: FastDepth 14 frames x 46 layers, MiDaS 12 frames x 136 layers, CPU + NPU-sim
Independent export check (5 checks, both models)
board_measured: FastDepth on the board, NPU + 4 cores, 5 Oct
MiDaS small on the board, NPU + 4 cores, 5 Oct
MiDaS small, same frame, CPU only
NPU output vs golden model (both models)
not_measured: Fmax on silicon (static timing says ~59 MHz)
flow_note: The conv layers (92 % of FastDepth's 180 M MACs, 98 % of MiDaS' 862 M MACs) run on the array; depthwise, upsample, bilinear, ReLU and skip-add on the CPU cores. The input replay buffer sends every input vector over APB once instead of once per 16 output channels; frame time is still limited by the APB link, not by the array (256 MACs per clock).
